rubrics.criterion: After the repair, the facts that describe how far a window is scrolled - the number of screen rows currently showing content, the screen row the primary cursor is displayed on, and the position relative to the whole file (the quantity behind the status bar percentage and the `All`/`Top`/`Bot` classification) - are computed by code on the view side of the tree: the module that owns `struct View` and its screen-line layout, not by the terminal backend, the Lua glue, the text-object adapter, or the status code.
rubrics.rationale: Every one of the four duplicated derivations in this instance computes the same viewport description from `win->view`; the central question of the task is where that description is produced.

rubrics.criterion: The scrollbar painter in the window-drawing code fills the last column from a scroll description obtained from view-owned code (or values derived only from such a description), and its body no longer iterates the view's screen-line list or queries the primary selection to derive used rows, the cursor's row, or the thumb interval by itself.
rubrics.rationale: The scrollbar was injected as the most mechanical duplication in ui-terminal.c; painters consuming geometry is the accepted refactor shape for this feature.

rubrics.criterion: The Lua `scrollinfo` binding marshals field values supplied by view-owned code: its body raises the values of the six documented fields (topline, lastline, lines, height, row, percent) into the Lua table without re-walking topline/lastline/selection or recomputing the percentage itself.
rubrics.rationale: A binding that ships the algorithm is one of the four manifestations of this case; after a sound repair it must be visible that vis-lua.c changed from compute-and-push to obtain-and-push.

rubrics.criterion: The screen-row text object in vis-text-objects.c no longer iterates screen lines to map a cursor position to a byte range; it delegates that mapping to view-owned code and its remaining body only adapts arguments and returns the range (including the empty-range handling).
rubrics.rationale: The text-object table entry dispatches through this adapter; the adapter is where wrapped-screen-row bookkeeping was misinjected and is the least discoverable of the four sites.

rubrics.criterion: Each distinct viewport fact has a single derivation site in the tree after the repair: no two functions among the four consumer areas (drawing, status composition, Lua binding, text-object adapter) contain a private copy of the used-rows walk, the cursor-row walk, or the scroll-position computation.
rubrics.rationale: Ownership is only restored if duplicates are actually dissolved; keeping two of the four copies would perpetuate the scattered knowledge this task targets.

rubrics.criterion: No consumer-side module keeps a function whose body still performs the viewport derivation under a different name or a thin delegation step (for example a renamed or wrapper-ified helper in ui-terminal.c/vis-lua.c/vis-text-objects.c whose body still walks the view internals, or a copy of the walk parked in a header or an unrelated module).
rubrics.rationale: Mechanical shape-shifting (renames, move-to-helper, static-inline in headers) is the plausible failure mode this instance must resist.

rubrics.criterion: The status line code that assembles the right-most segment is rewired to obtain the indicator/scroll facts from view-owned code, and no status-side call asks a UI-side helper to compute viewport facts any more, i.e. the inverted dependency between the windowing module (view.c's window_status_update) and the backend introduced by this feature is gone.
rubrics.rationale: The injected call chain crosses from view.c back into ui-terminal.c to have the UI compute view knowledge; freeing the status path from that inversion is coupled work a correct repair cannot skip.

rubrics.criterion: Declarations introduced or moved by the repair live in the header of the module that implements them (scroll/viewport queries and their result types on the view side, not declared in backend or UI headers), and the consumer modules include what they use without new struct-field bloat in window/view headers.
rubrics.rationale: The editor places internal declarations per owner (view.h carries the view API, ui.h the backend API); a repair that misplaces its new declarations restores a layering smell, not a fix.

rubrics.criterion: All four features remain wired end to end: the window drawing path still invokes the scrollbar painter, the status refresh still appends the indicator segment, the Lua window method table still registers scrollinfo (and its embedded LDoc comment still matches the implemented fields), and the text-object id enum value and dispatch-table entry still invoke the screen-row object.
rubrics.rationale: Complete unwinding must not strand registration: the tables and call paths that make the features reachable are spread across four modules and each has to survive the reorganization.

rubrics.criterion: Functions in consumer modules that existed only to perform the duplicated derivation are deleted outright (definition and forward declaration, including the ui.h declaration of the UI-side indicator composer), rather than kept around as dead or redundant code.
rubrics.rationale: The injected UI-side helpers exist solely for this task's scattered walk; if they remain after the repair, the codebase carries twice the entry points for the same knowledge.

rubrics.criterion: The final tree contains no unreachable leftovers from the removed arrangement: no declaration for a function that no longer exists, no unused local buffers/variables that existed only to receive the old on-the-spot computations, and no second retained copy of the walk kept 'just in case' behind an option, a comment, or a conditional.
rubrics.rationale: Half-done cleanups in this instance would leave readers (and the window flow) with vestigial state that suggests a wrong history of the code.

rubrics.criterion: Scroll reporting behaves identically at the boundaries: with the entire file visible, the status indicator is `All`; with the file start at the top of the viewport and the cursor on the first screen row, it is `Top`; with the file end within the viewport, it is `Bot`; otherwise it is a 1..100 percentage with a trailing `%` matching the cursor position; and the Lua scrollinfo percentage stays consistent (within +/-1 or identically equal) with what the status segment shows for the same window.
rubrics.rationale: The All/Top/Bot classification and percent are this instance's user-visible contract, encoded in the existing test/smoke behavior; a repair must be equivalent, not a re-specification.

rubrics.criterion: The scrollbar is still rendered at the right edge of each window during window drawing on the curses build - track bounded by used rows, thumb over the visible slice, cursor highlight at the cursor's screen row - without writing outside the window's cell area, and an empty or single-line viewport degenerates gracefully (no one-pixel negative intervals, division by zero, or off-screen writes).
rubrics.rationale: The injected painter has explicit degenerate cases (zero-size text, view subdivisions, height 1); a careless ownership move is most likely to break precisely those.

rubrics.criterion: The screen-row object's byte range is unchanged for wrapped views: for a cursor on a wrapped line the range covers all continuation screen rows of the same file line within the viewport, for the first displayed row it starts at the viewport start byte, and positions outside the displayed area map to an empty range usable by operators without corrupting text.
rubrics.rationale: This text object encodes the most intricate viewport bookkeeping of the four (line-number equality across wrapped rows, clamping at the bottom line); its observable range is the regression tell for the delegation.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not reach beyond the scroll-feature consumers and their new view-side home: it leaves text storage, syntax highlighting, file/marks, registers, and window sizing behavior untouched, and does not widen the scripting API or embed new public contracts beyond what plugins already used.
rubrics.rationale: With four consumer modules in play a broad repair is tempting; scope discipline separates an ownership fix from an opportunistic rewrite.

rubrics.criterion: The Lua API surface is preserved exactly: scripts written against the pre-repair `win:scrollinfo()` documentation still run, the method name and the six integer field names (topline, lastline, lines, height, row, percent) and their value types are identical, and file/window/registry bindings outside this feature are unmodified.
rubrics.rationale: Script compatibility is the packaging-level contract of this feature; a rename or field swap would silently break user plugins and the documented binding.
